prompt:
An interior photograph of this open-plan office floor, looking south-east from the west end of the open-plan north zone: 5 bench desk positions with task chairs straight ahead, full-height glazed meeting-room partitions on the right, a SERVICES RISER on the left.

General material and lighting reference (use unless contradicted below):
Material and lighting style: board-formed fair-faced concrete soffit left fully exposed, beams and formwork marks reading clearly; large square luminous grid panels suspended on slim rods below it, with slim black track spotlights alongside. Matt white walls, and one full-height wall in warm honey-toned cork carrying thin white display shelves. Bench tables in pale oak with thick square edges; a slim white rail running above the table tops. Chairs in black mesh and leather on polished aluminium five-star bases. Seamless mid-grey micro-cement floor, with a woven light-grey carpet laid under the desk zone. Meeting room enclosed in clear glass with light oak frames and white horizontal venetian blinds. Strong soft daylight from one side; artificial light warm neutral, around 3500 K.

Interior architectural photography, 24 mm tilt-shift lens, two-point perspective with perfectly straight vertical lines, even artificial ceiling lighting only — no daylight source is in shot, realistic material response, natural dynamic range, crisp detail, no text, no signage, no CG or 3D-render look.

FIXED DESIGN DECISIONS — these override anything above, follow every line exactly:
· acoustic ceiling rafts floating over the desk bands, with the painted soffit and services exposed over the circulation
· white horizontal venetian blinds with the slats half open
· large square luminous grid panels suspended on slim rods below the soffit, glowing evenly, with slim black track spotlights alongside
· plain light grey vinyl flooring
· light oak and white furniture with simple square-edge profiles
· no desk screens at all, plain open bench desks
· a warm timber and neutral palette
· no people in the frame

MEASURED FROM THE BUILDING DRAWINGS — these are facts, not preferences. Never change them, whatever the reference photograph or the style description shows:
· NO exterior window and NO glazed facade is visible in this frame — the camera looks away from the facade, into the depth of the floor. Do NOT add a window, a glazed exterior wall, a bright daylight opening or a view out anywhere in this frame, however much the style reference or a typical office photograph suggests one. Every wall you can see here is solid or an internal partition. The light in this frame is artificial.
· Ceiling height above the finished floor: 3000 mm. Do not lower it.
· Main aisle 1800 mm, secondary aisles 1400 mm. Do not narrow them.
· This frame contains at least 5 clearly readable workstations (one desk position plus one task chair each), with more receding into the distance. Show no fewer than that, and do not close the room off with a wall that is not in the reference, shorten it, or thin out the desk rows.
· Down the right of this frame runs a GLAZED INTERNAL PARTITION, not a solid wall: 4 tall glass panes in slim frames, floor up to 2900 mm, with a glazed transom over the doors. Paint it as clear glass with the enclosed room readable through it — a meeting room INSIDE the building, lit by its own ceiling lights. It is not a window: never put daylight, sky or a view of the outdoors behind it. Reading it as blank wall is the single worst mistake here.
· Down the left of this frame, taking about 3% of the frame, is a SERVICES RISER: a flush metal access door with no visible handle, painted to match the wall. The massing model shows it as blank wall only because the door is not modelled — the door is really there, so put it in. Never leave that wall blank.
· Across the frame ahead of you, taking about 3% of the frame, is a small service room: one flush single door. The massing model shows it as blank wall only because the door is not modelled — the door is really there, so put it in. Never leave that wall blank.

The reference image is an UNTEXTURED WHITE MASSING MODEL — every surface is placeholder grey, there is no material, colour or lighting information in it whatsoever. Take ONLY the geometry, camera and object positions from it. Invent all materials, colours, textures and lighting yourself, strictly following the fixed design decisions below.

The reference image is a SIMPLIFIED MASSING MODEL, not a finished render. Every plain block in it is a placeholder standing for a real object at that exact position, size and orientation. Replace each placeholder with properly detailed real-world furniture and fittings: ergonomic mesh-back task chairs with contoured seats, adjustable armrests, gas lift and five-star castor bases; bench desk systems with slim square legs, under-desk cable trays and cable grommets; slim-bezel monitors on articulated arms, keyboards and mice; a few believable personal items. Keep unchanged: the camera and framing, the room shape, the number of desks and chairs, the aisle widths and the ceiling height. The dark outlines drawn along every edge of the reference are annotation lines, not real edges of real objects — reproduce none of them; the finished photograph must contain no drawn outlines anywhere. Likewise its flat untextured grey surfaces are placeholders for materials you must invent, not a colour to keep. Do not colour in the massing model — re-photograph the same room. The result must read as a photograph of a completed, occupied office — never as a 3D render, never as line art or a coloured drawing, never with blocky simplified furniture.
